newsitem.title: INDIA: India phone, postal workers strike in fifth day.
newsitem.headline: India phone, postal workers strike in fifth day.

text.p: A five-day old strike which has crippled India's phone and postal services will continue until the government gives a written assurance to meet workers' demands, trade unions said on Sunday.

The unions, three representing postal workers and three telecommunication workers, say Communications Minister Beni Prasad Varma's promise to consider their demand for the elimination of a 3,500-rupee ($100) cap on annual pay bonuses was not enough.

"If the minister is willing to say in a cabinet meeting that the ceiling will be abolished and gives it in a written statement only then the strike would be withdrawn," said Rishi Kumar, treasurer of the Bharatiya Telecom Employees Union.

A cabinet meeting is not scheduled until Tuesday. But the unions, with backing from one million workers, said that they are willing to budge if Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda, steps in to resolve the dispute on Sunday or Monday.

"The postal unions have said that without a cabinet meeting it would be impossible to do anything. We say if the minister or somebody on behalf of the prime minister comes forward, we are willing to consider the issue," Kumar told Reuters.
The government, concerned over high interest rates and the cost of debt, had set itself an ambitious budget tightening target this year through a ceiling on bonus payments.
On the first day of the strike, Varma called the work stoppage illegal, saying the unions had not given adequate advance notice.
The strike has crippled government postal services with millions of letters piling up in post offices across the nation.
Telecommunications services, which are largely automated, have fared better, but operator-related services and repair and maintenance have been disrupted.
